prediction.likelyOutcome: Montgomery Park is more likely than not to prevail at the bench trial on the core liability question — that NCO failed to satisfy the early-termination conditions and remains liable under the lease — given its contemporaneous notice of non-compliance and NCO's unilateral vacatur over that objection. On that basis, Montgomery Park should recover at least the $313,662.76 in unpaid rent documented in its July 2011 default letter, likely more once post-2011 accruals and default-rate interest are accounted for, plus contractual attorney's fees as the prevailing party, while NCO's overcharge, unjust enrichment, and fraud counterclaims face significant doctrinal hurdles and are unlikely to produce a large offset on this record.

outcome.description: After a bench trial the district court entered judgment for Montgomery Park on its past-due-rent counterclaim of $9,854,566.95 plus postjudgment interest (upheld in earlier Fourth Circuit appeals at 842 F.3d 816, 918 F.3d 388 and 40 F.4th 123). The court then awarded $2,074,379.88 in attorneys' fees and nontaxable expenses, $115,942.10 taxable costs and $1,576,036.07 default interest ($3,766,358.05 total). In this fifth appeal the Fourth Circuit affirmed the fee/cost award (including expert fees) but vacated the default-interest component, holding interest runs only from the August 24, 2022 demand, and remanded for recalculation; the underlying rent judgment was not disturbed.
